article.title: The model is coming
article.subtitle: A quick update on plans for a busy political week.

extraction.summary: A short signposting post announcing that the Silver Bulletin 2024 presidential election model is about 90 percent complete, with launch targeted for roughly Wednesday, June 26, 2024. The remaining work is mostly edge cases such as handling ranked choice voting in Maine. Polling averages will be free, while forecast probabilities will be paywalled. Updates will be about weekly at first and will speed up as the election nears. Silver claims the model is the best available and the only one with a long-term track record, and he previews a June presidential debate reaction post.

findings.statement: The Silver Bulletin 2024 presidential model includes explicit handling of ranked choice voting in Maine. Silver describes this as one of the remaining edge cases during development.
findings.evidence_quote: mostly down to edge-case stuff like handling ranked choice voting in Maine

findings.statement: Updates to the Silver Bulletin 2024 presidential forecast were planned for about once a week at launch, becoming more frequent as election day approaches.

quantities.name: initial update frequency
quantities.context: Early phase of the 2024 forecast after the late-June launch

findings.rationale: Silver describes a "slow food" approach and wants to keep the model from consuming all his other newsletter work.
findings.evidence_quote: with updates once a week or so initially before accelerating as the election approaches

findings.statement: For the 2024 Silver Bulletin presidential model, the polling averages are publicly available. The forecast component and its win probabilities are paywalled.
findings.rationale: Silver wants a smaller, self-selected audience, wants to avoid 'model wars' dynamics, and expects better economics.
findings.evidence_quote: I deliberately want a smaller, self-selected audience and to avoid too many "model wars"-type dynamics

findings.statement: Silver says the 2024 Silver Bulletin presidential model is the only forecast with a long-term track record. This implies continuity with the models he built in the FiveThirtyEight era.
findings.evidence_quote: it's the only one that has any sort of long-term track record

findings.statement: As of June 22, 2024, the Silver Bulletin presidential model was about 90 percent complete. Launch was targeted for Wednesday, plus or minus a day, which would be around June 26, 2024. It was built with help from elections analyst Eli McKown-Dawson.
findings.evidence_quote: work on the presidential election model is about 90 percent done

political_insights.insight: The first 2024 presidential debate was scheduled unusually early, in late June. Silver flags this as unusual.
political_insights.forecasting_implication: Debate effects in 2024 arrive earlier than in the historical calendar, which may matter for any debate-bounce handling.
